\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جريمة} (jarīma)}{جريمة (jarīma)}]{\ar{جريمة} (jarīma) — a crime}

\label{lesson:AR-C300-jarima}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to mention, then the Arabic for to pass on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جريمة}}
\textbf{\ar{جريمة}} — \emph{jarīma} — \textquotedblleft{}a crime\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وقعت} \ar{جريمة} \ar{في} \ar{الحي} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waqaʿat jarīma fī al-ḥayy ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A crime took place in the neighbourhood yesterday.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جريمة}} (\emph{jarīma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-r-m} (Lane), first \textquotedblleft{}to cut off (dates from the palm)\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}to commit a crime\textquotedblright{}; \emph{jurm} is a wrong done.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jarīma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jarīma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waqaʿat jarīma fī al-ḥayy ams.} — A crime took place in the neighbourhood yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to mention, then the Arabic for to pass on, then say \emph{jarīma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{جريمة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A crime\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مجرم} (mujrim)}{مجرم (mujrim)}]{\ar{مجرم} (mujrim) — a criminal}

\label{lesson:AR-C300-mujrim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to pass on, then the Arabic for a crime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مجرم}}
\textbf{\ar{مجرم}} — \emph{mujrim} — \textquotedblleft{}a criminal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هرب} \ar{المجرم} \ar{من} \ar{الشرطة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{haraba al-mujrim min ash-shurṭa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The criminal ran away from the police.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{مجرمون}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مجرم}} (\emph{mujrim}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-r-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to commit a crime\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Mujrim} is the Form IV participle, \textquotedblleft{}one who commits a crime\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujrim}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujrim}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haraba al-mujrim min ash-shurṭa.} — The criminal ran away from the police.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to pass on, then the Arabic for a crime, then say \emph{mujrim} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مجرم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A criminal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لص} (liṣṣ)}{لص (liṣṣ)}]{\ar{لص} (liṣṣ) — a thief}

\label{lesson:AR-C300-liss}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a crime, then the Arabic for a criminal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لص}}
\textbf{\ar{لص}} — \emph{liṣṣ} — \textquotedblleft{}a thief\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{دخل} \ar{لص} \ar{البيت} \ar{في} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dakhala liṣṣ al-bayt fī al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A thief got into the house at night.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{لصوص}, \emph{luṣūṣ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لص}} (\emph{liṣṣ}) is filed by Lane under the root \emph{l-ṣ-ṣ}, with the plural \emph{luṣūṣ}. It was borrowed from Greek \emph{lēistēs}, a robber (EtymDB); the path it took into Arabic is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{liṣṣ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{liṣṣ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dakhala liṣṣ al-bayt fī al-layl.} — A thief got into the house at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a crime, then the Arabic for a criminal, then say \emph{liṣṣ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{لص} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A thief\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سرق} (saraqa)}{سرق (saraqa)}]{\ar{سرق} (saraqa) — to steal}

\label{lesson:AR-C300-saraqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a criminal, then the Arabic for a thief.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سرق}}
\textbf{\ar{سرق}} — \emph{saraqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to steal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سرق} \ar{اللص} \ar{حقيبة} \ar{السيدة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saraqa al-liṣṣ ḥaqībat as-sayyida.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief stole the lady’s bag.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يسرق}, \emph{yasriq}.

The passive \ar{سرق}, \emph{suriqa}, is common: \ar{سرقت} \ar{سيارتي}, my car was stolen.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سرق}} (\emph{saraqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-r-q} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to take a thing secretly\textquotedblright{}; \emph{sariqa} is theft and \emph{sāriq} a thief.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saraqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saraqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saraqa al-liṣṣ ḥaqībat as-sayyida.} — The thief stole the lady’s bag.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a criminal, then the Arabic for a thief, then say \emph{saraqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{سرق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To steal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اعتقل} (iʿtaqala)}{اعتقل (iʿtaqala)}]{\ar{اعتقل} (iʿtaqala) — to arrest, to detain}

\label{lesson:AR-C300-itaqala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a thief, then the Arabic for to steal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اعتقل}}
\textbf{\ar{اعتقل}} — \emph{iʿtaqala} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrest, to detain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اعتقلت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{الرجل} \ar{في} \ar{المطار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iʿtaqalat ash-shurṭa ar-rajul fī al-maṭār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police arrested the man at the airport.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعتقل}, \emph{yaʿtaqil}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اعتقل}} (\emph{iʿtaqala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-q-l} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to tie up a camel's foreleg\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{ʿaql}, the mind that holds one back. Form VIII \emph{iʿtaqala} is \textquotedblleft{}to hold a person in\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtaqala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtaqala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtaqalat ash-shurṭa ar-rajul fī al-maṭār.} — The police arrested the man at the airport.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a thief, then the Arabic for to steal, then say \emph{iʿtaqala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اعتقل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To arrest, to detain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{News and stories — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R300-review-293-300}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a correspondent and a statement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a correspondent, a statement, a gazette, to announce, to declare
  \item suddenly, to take place, to explode, at first, at that moment
  \item a tale, to narrate, to tell a story, to recount, one day
  \item journalism, an editor, an article, to edit, a bulletin
  \item a radio station, a channel, a radio set, to put on air, on air
  \item a blaze, smoke, to catch fire, to burn down, a firefighter
  \item meanwhile, later on, the next day, to mention, to pass on
  \item a crime, a criminal, a thief, to steal, to arrest
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A correspondent? (\textbf{\ar{مراسل}}, \emph{murāsil}.) A statement? (\textbf{\ar{بيان}}, \emph{bayān}.) A gazette? (\textbf{\ar{صحيفة}}, \emph{ṣaḥīfa}.) To announce? (\textbf{\ar{أعلن}}, \emph{aʿlana}.) To declare? (\textbf{\ar{صرح}}, \emph{ṣarraḥa}.) Suddenly? (\textbf{\ar{فجأة}}, \emph{fajʾatan}.) To take place? (\textbf{\ar{وقع}}, \emph{waqaʿa}.) To explode? (\textbf{\ar{انفجر}}, \emph{infajara}.) At first? (\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{البداية}}, \emph{fī al-bidāya}.) At that moment? (\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة}}, \emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa}.) A tale? (\textbf{\ar{حكاية}}, \emph{ḥikāya}.) To narrate? (\textbf{\ar{روى}}, \emph{rawā}.) To tell a story? (\textbf{\ar{قص}}, \emph{qaṣṣa}.) To recount? (\textbf{\ar{سرد}}, \emph{sarada}.) One day? (\textbf{\ar{ذات} \ar{يوم}}, \emph{dhāta yawm}.) Journalism? (\textbf{\ar{صحافة}}, \emph{ṣaḥāfa}.) An editor? (\textbf{\ar{محرر}}, \emph{muḥarrir}.) An article? (\textbf{\ar{مقال}}, \emph{maqāl}.) To edit? (\textbf{\ar{حرر}}, \emph{ḥarrara}.) A bulletin? (\textbf{\ar{نشرة}}, \emph{nashra}.) A radio station? (\textbf{\ar{إذاعة}}, \emph{idhāʿa}.) A channel? (\textbf{\ar{قناة}}, \emph{qanāh}.) A radio set? (\textbf{\ar{مذياع}}, \emph{midhyāʿ}.) To put on air? (\textbf{\ar{أذاع}}, \emph{adhāʿa}.) On air? (\textbf{\ar{على} \ar{الهواء}}, \emph{ʿalā al-hawāʾ}.) A blaze? (\textbf{\ar{حريق}}, \emph{ḥarīq}.) Smoke? (\textbf{\ar{دخان}}, \emph{dukhān}.) To catch fire? (\textbf{\ar{اشتعل}}, \emph{ishtaʿala}.) To burn down? (\textbf{\ar{احترق}}, \emph{iḥtaraqa}.) A firefighter? (\textbf{\ar{رجل} \ar{إطفاء}}, \emph{rajul iṭfāʾ}.) Meanwhile? (\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{هذه} \ar{الأثناء}}, \emph{fī hādhihi al-athnāʾ}.) Later on? (\textbf{\ar{فيما} \ar{بعد}}, \emph{fīmā baʿd}.) The next day? (\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{اليوم} \ar{التالي}}, \emph{fī al-yawm at-tālī}.) To mention? (\textbf{\ar{ذكر}}, \emph{dhakara}.) To pass on? (\textbf{\ar{نقل}}, \emph{naqala}.) A crime? (\textbf{\ar{جريمة}}, \emph{jarīma}.) A criminal? (\textbf{\ar{مجرم}}, \emph{mujrim}.) A thief? (\textbf{\ar{لص}}, \emph{liṣṣ}.) To steal? (\textbf{\ar{سرق}}, \emph{saraqa}.) To arrest? (\textbf{\ar{اعتقل}}, \emph{iʿtaqala}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
